titulo.texto: Tablet of the Cross of Palenque

frase_gancho.texto: A boy and a grown king, the same man, on either side of a sacred cross.

puente_narrativo.texto: From Palenque we move on to the palace of another kingdom, on the banks of the Usumacinta River. Look for a stone relief with two figures facing each other: a king and a queen who hands him a jaguar helmet.

guion_corto.texto: A six-year-old boy and a grown king appear on the same stone, and they are the same man: Kan Bahlam, son and successor of [Pakal](mna_s09_mascara_pakal). It is a large limestone panel from the Cross Group of Palenque, a Maya work of the Late Classic, carved around the year 692. Specialists read in it two moments of his life: as a child, when he was presented as heir, an event of the year 641, and as an adult, when he received power, in the year 684. At the center rises a sacred plant in the shape of a cross. On the sides, columns of glyphs tell who he was and why it was his turn to rule. It is a political argument carved in stone.

guion_largo.texto:
Imagine that your father, the most famous king in the city, has just died, and now it falls to you to rule. How do you convince everyone that you have the right? Kan Bahlam, the son of [Pakal](mna_s09_mascara_pakal), did it with a stone: he ordered this panel carved and placed it in the most sacred spot of a temple.

It is a Maya work of the Late Classic, carved around the year 692 in limestone. It comes from Palenque, in Chiapas, from the Cross Group, a complex of three temples: the Temple of the Cross, the Temple of the Sun and the Temple of the Foliated Cross. Each one kept in its inner sanctuary a large panel like this one, with a scene and a text that were read as a single message.

Look at the figures. The king appears twice: as a child, at six years old, and as an adult. According to the specialists’ reading, the scene of the child recalls the year 641, when he was presented as heir; the one of the adult, the year 684, when he received the insignia of power, only a few months after his father’s death. Forty-three years passed between one moment and the other, and the stone joins them in a single image, as if everything had been decided from the very beginning.

Between the two figures rises a sacred plant in the shape of a cross. For the Maya it was not a Christian symbol: it was the axis of the world, a tree or a maize plant that joined the underworld, the earth and the sky. These crosses were carved long before the Spaniards arrived, and that is why we call it a “cross” only because of its shape.

On the sides run the texts, entire columns of glyphs. This is the most important part, though the hardest to see. They tell that, according to the tradition of Palenque, the protective gods of the city had been born in mythical times, and that the king was their heir on earth. In this way, Kan Bahlam’s personal story was joined to that of the gods of his city, and his right to rule seemed as ancient as the universe.

Think of it as a political poster, but carved to last. Today’s rulers use speeches, advertisements and social media; Kan Bahlam used limestone, sculptors and several years of work. And it worked: more than one thousand three hundred years later, his name has reached you.

If you are coming from the [crypt of Pakal](mna_s09_cripta_pakal), you already know the father: the king whose face was covered in jade. Here you meet the son, the one who inherited the city and ruled until the year 702. In those years he built this complex of temples to make it clear that the dynasty was still standing. One tomb for the father and three temples for the son: the story of a family, told in two kinds of stone.

Before moving on, compare the two figures of the king. What changes in the body, the headdress and the posture of the child and the adult? On this stone time does not pass: the boy and the king are one and the same.

texto: Find the two portraits of the king: one as a child and one as an adult
Find the sacred plant in the shape of a cross between them
Look at the columns of glyphs on the sides: they are the text that explains the scene

texto.pregunta: Myth: The cross on the panel is a Christian symbol that arrived with the Spaniards.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It is a sacred Maya plant or tree in the shape of a cross, carved around the year 692, long before the Spaniards arrived.
